To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we introduce a novel framework for improving the sample efficiency of reinforcement learning algorithms, AG-RL, and show that it improves the performance in 19 out of the 21 Atari 2600 games tested.

(1) AG-RL can improve the sample efficiency and performance of a model-based RL agent in 100% of tested Atari games, (2) AG-RL with SAC can outperform the state-of-the-art model-free agent on 90% of tested Atari tasks in terms of sample efficiency, and (3) the sample efficiency of AG-RL can be further improved using a novel, simple, and effective method of action selection that we call "action selection via action selection"
AG-DDQN and AG-SAC improve performance in Atari games and AG-SAC improves sample efficiency in Atari games.

the question: "How can we use the concept of grammatical structure in action to improve sample efficiency in reinforcement learning agents?".

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AG-DDQN is a very strong baseline and that AG-SAC is the best method for sample efficiency on Atari.
AG-RL improves the sample efficiency of both model-free and model-based RL algorithms.
AG-RL is a promising approach that has the potential to improve performance in a wide range of RL problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we show that AG-DDQN and AG-SAC improve performance in 27 out of 28 tested Atari games (AG-DDQN: median +31%, max 668%, AG-SAC: median +96%, max +3,756%); and that AG-SAC improves the sample efficiency of SAC in 17 out 20 tested games (median +63%, maximum +13.140%).
AG-DDQN and AG-SAC are both sample efficient, perform well on the Atari 100k benchmarks, and are competitive with the state-of-the-art.
AG-RL is a simple yet effective method for improving sample efficiency in RL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AG-RL is a simple and powerful method for improving sample efficiency in reinforcement learning.
the sample efficiency of RL agents can be substantially increased by leveraging hierarchical action representations.

the AG-RL framework provides a general and simple way for improving sample efficiency of RL agents, and that this framework is particularly useful for improving sample efficiency for discrete action RL agents.
